key_insight: A small, clinically meaningful set of community-available features enabled zero-shot LLMs to screen chronic kidney disease more effectively than using all features.
clinical_relevance: This approach could make early CKD screening more practical in low-resource or community settings by reducing the need for extensive tests or dataset-specific training.
method: Selected a compact subset of clinically relevant variables using ML-based feature analysis.
Serialized tabular patient records into standardized text prompts for zero-shot LLM inference.
Compared four LLMs across full vs selected feature sets on three heterogeneous CKD datasets from three countries.
evidence_signal: Across models and datasets, the selected feature set produced consistent, statistically significant gains in balanced accuracy and probability estimates, with performance described as suitable for screening.
watch_item: Performance still depends on careful feature selection and external validation, and real-world deployment may face population shift and prompt/input standardization challenges.
paper_title: From Many to Meaningful: Feature-Guided Zero-Shot Chronic Kidney Disease Screening Using Large Language Models
